content: Hi! How can I help you today with your SQL queries?
Hi, I need to join our customers and orders tables to make a report. Can you help me write that query?
Absolutely. Before I proceed, could you tell me which SQL dialect you're using (Postgres, MySQL, BigQuery, or Snowflake)?
We're using Postgres.

Great! In Postgres, here's a basic query to join customers and orders:
```sql
SELECT c.customer_id, c.name, o.order_id, o.order_date
FROM customers c
JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id;
```
Thanks! How can I include only orders from 2023?

You can filter by order_date using the WHERE clause:
```sql
SELECT c.customer_id, c.name, o.order_id, o.order_date
FROM customers c
JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
WHERE o.order_date >= '2023-01-01' AND o.order_date < '2024-01-01';
```
Nice. Could you add the total order amount too? The column is called total_amount in orders.

Certainly. Here's the updated query:
```sql
SELECT c.customer_id, c.name, o.order_id, o.order_date, o.total_amount
FROM customers c
JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
WHERE o.order_date >= '2023-01-01' AND o.order_date < '2024-01-01';
```
Is there a way to sort the results by total_amount, highest first?

Yes, just add ORDER BY:
```sql
SELECT c.customer_id, c.name, o.order_id, o.order_date, o.total_amount
FROM customers c
JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
WHERE o.order_date >= '2023-01-01' AND o.order_date < '2024-01-01'
ORDER BY o.total_amount DESC;
```
How do I show only customers with more than 3 orders in 2023?

You can use GROUP BY and HAVING to filter by order count:
```sql
SELECT c.customer_id, c.name, COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count
FROM customers c
JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
WHERE o.order_date >= '2023-01-01' AND o.order_date < '2024-01-01'
GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.name
HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) > 3;
```
Great, can I get the total amount per customer as well?

Absolutely! Here's the query with total amount summed per customer:
```sql
SELECT c.customer_id, c.name, COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent
FROM customers c
JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
WHERE o.order_date >= '2023-01-01' AND o.order_date < '2024-01-01'
GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.name
HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) > 3;
```
Suppose I want to see the top 5 customers by total_spent for 2023. How do I do that?

Just add ORDER BY and LIMIT:
```sql
SELECT c.customer_id, c.name, COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent
FROM customers c
JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
WHERE o.order_date >= '2023-01-01' AND o.order_date < '2024-01-01'
GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.name
ORDER BY total_spent DESC
LIMIT 5;
```
Perfect! One last thing, can I see the average order value for each of these customers?

Of course. You can calculate it with AVG():
```sql
SELECT c.customer_id, c.name, COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent, AVG(o.total_amount) AS avg_order_value
FROM customers c
JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
WHERE o.order_date >= '2023-01-01' AND o.order_date < '2024-01-01'
GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.name
ORDER BY total_spent DESC
LIMIT 5;
```
That covers everything. Thanks for the help!
